<ran command="adi-mono tasks show FULL-STACK-FASTAPI-1" status="ok">
FULL-STACK-FASTAPI-1 — RBAC: user<->role<->permission access control (Admin/Manager/Member) [blocked]
  status: open · project: full-stack-fastapi · cwd: /Users/mgorunuch/.adi/mono/projects/full-stack-fastapi/workspaces/main · subtasks: 3/3 open
  GOAL
Add role-aware access control (RBAC) to the Full-Stack FastAPI template. Implement a
user <-> role <-> permission relation in the DB, enforce authorization in the backend,
reflect the same rules in the frontend, add a short-lived (<5min) server-side permission
cache that is invalidated on changes, and migrate the existing `is_superuser` model into a
role with permission "super". Three access levels: Admin, Manager, Member.

LOCKED ARCHITECTURE (contract — all specialists build to this)

Permissions (atomic string names):
  - super        : unrestricted; a holder passes EVERY permission check (back-compat for old superuser)
  - users:read   : list/view any user; view roles list
  - users:manage : create/update/delete users AND change their role assignments ("manage access")
  - metrics:read : view metrics page/endpoint

Roles (seeded, by name):
  - admin   -> {super, users:read, users:manage, metrics:read}
  - manager -> {users:read, metrics:read}
  - member  -> {}   (baseline self-service only: own profile, own password, own items — no special perm)

DB schema (SQLModel, new tables):
  - Permission(id uuid pk, name str unique index, description str|None)
  - Role(id uuid pk, name str unique index, description str|None)
  - RolePermission(role_id fk->role pk, permission_id fk->permission pk)   # M2M
  - UserRole(user_id fk->user pk, role_id fk->role pk)                     # M2M
  - User: DROP the stored `is_superuser` column; add roles: list[Role] via UserRole.

is_superuser compatibility (critical for migration safety + existing tests):
  - UserCreate.is_superuser (default False) stays accepted as INPUT; True => assign admin role on create.
    UserUpdate.is_superuser (optional) stays accepted; True => add admin role, False => remove super-bearing role(s).
    (This keeps init_db(..., is_superuser=True), routes/private.py, and existing tests working.)
  - Add role_ids: list[uuid] | None to UserCreate/UserUpdate for explicit role assignment (admin-only path).
  - UserPublic exposes is_superuser as a COMPUTED field = ("super" in resolved permissions),
    plus new fields roles: list[str] (role names) and permissions: list[str] (resolved perm names).
  - Self-protection "superusers can't delete themselves" => "users with `super` permission can't delete themselves."

Authorization layer (backend/app/api/deps.py):
  - get_current_user unchanged (loads fresh user each request, 400 if inactive) — this already makes
    active-status changes affect existing sessions.
  - resolve_permissions(session, user) -> set[str], served through the cache (below).
  - require_permission(perm) dependency factory: 403 unless perm in resolved perms OR "super" present.
  - Keep get_current_active_superuser == require_permission("super") for back-compat.

Route authorization changes (backend/app/api/routes/users.py etc.):
  - GET  /users/            -> users:read     (admin+manager; member 403; anon 401)
  - POST /users/            -> users:manage   (admin only)
  - PATCH /users/{id}       -> users:manage   (admin only; accepts role_ids)
  - DELETE /users/{id}      -> users:manage   (admin only)
  - GET  /users/{id}        -> self always OK; otherwise users:read
  - POST /utils/test-email  -> keep super (admin only)
  - password-recovery-html-content -> keep super
  - NEW GET /roles/         -> users:read (role selector for admin UI)
  - NEW GET /metrics/ (own router) -> metrics:read (admin+manager). Simple stub: counts (total users,
    active users, users per role). Member 403, anon 401.
  - /users/me, /users/me/password, DELETE /users/me, items/* ownership -> unchanged (member self-service).
  - PATCH /users/me must NOT allow changing roles/permissions/is_superuser (UserUpdateMe has no such fields) — assert this.

Short-lived permission cache (new module, e.g. backend/app/core/permissions.py):
  - In-process TTL cache: user_id -> (frozenset[str] perms, expires_at). TTL default 60s
    (settings.PERMISSIONS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, well under the 5-min requirement). threading.Lock guarded.
  - invalidate_user(user_id) on: user update, role assignment change, deactivation, deletion.
  - invalidate_all() available for role->permission changes.
  - Document the single-process limitation (multi-worker would need Redis) — do NOT implement Redis (scope).

Session/access invalidation requirements (must be true & tested):
  - Deactivating a user -> their existing JWT yields 400 on next request.
  - Demoting a manager to member -> next GET /users/ is 403 (cache invalidated on change, not after TTL).
  - Promoting a member to manager -> next GET /users/ is 200.

Migration (alembic; down_revision = fe56fa70289e, the current head):
  - upgrade(): create permission/role/rolepermission/userrole tables; data-migrate seed the 3 roles,
    4 permissions, and their links; backfill userrole from existing users.is_superuser
    (True->admin, False->member); then DROP users.is_superuser.
  - downgrade(): add is_superuser column back, backfill True for users with admin/super role, drop link tables + role + permission.
  - Must be safe against a populated DB.

Reviewer local exercise:
  - Seed demo users in development only (idempotent, dev-gated): manager@example.com and member@example.com
    with password "changethis" alongside the existing admin@example.com. Document the three logins.

Tests (security-critical focus) — see child task for the checklist. Existing suite (58 tests) MUST stay green.

SEQUENCING
  1. fsf-backend: tests-first (author RBAC checklist) -> model -> migration -> cache -> enforcement -> green.
  2. fsf-frontend: once backend OpenAPI is stable, regenerate client + reflect rules + guard routes + role UI + metrics stub.
  3. fsf-secops: security review of the whole change.

Baseline: existing backend suite is GREEN (58 passed) as of start. FASTAPI_ENV=development, DB at :8071.

FULL-STACK-FASTAPI-2 — Backend RBAC — tests-first, then model/migration/cache/enforcement [ready]
  status: open · project: full-stack-fastapi · parent: FULL-STACK-FASTAPI-1 · cwd: /Users/mgorunuch/.adi/mono/projects/full-stack-fastapi/workspaces/main
  Owner: fsf-backend. Build to the LOCKED ARCHITECTURE in the parent task FULL-STACK-FASTAPI-1.
Work TEST-FIRST, in small verifiable steps, from backend/.

START FROM THE TESTS (deliver the checklist first):
Author a focused RBAC test suite that encodes the contract and serves as the strict checklist.
Put the new tests in backend/tests/api/routes/test_rbac.py (+ a cache unit test, e.g.
backend/tests/core/test_permissions_cache.py). Add helpers to backend/tests/utils/user.py for
creating a user with given role names and getting their auth headers.

The checklist (each an assertion / test):
  1. Seed integrity: roles admin/manager/member exist with exactly the parent's permission sets.
  2. /users/me returns roles + permissions + computed is_superuser for admin/manager/member.
  3. GET /users/      : admin 200, manager 200, member 403, anon 401.
  4. POST /users/     : admin ok, manager 403, member 403.
  5. PATCH /users/{id}: admin ok, manager 403, member 403.
  6. DELETE /users/{id}: admin ok, manager 403, member 403.
  7. GET /users/{id}  : self 200 for all; other-user -> admin/manager 200, member 403.
  8. Role assignment (users:manage): admin can set a user's role_ids via PATCH; manager 403;
     a manager CANNOT escalate self to admin.
  9. GET /metrics/    : admin 200, manager 200, member 403, anon 401.
 10. Member self-service preserved: GET/PATCH /users/me, change password, own items CRUD.
 11. PATCH /users/me ignores/rejects any attempt to change role/permission/is_superuser.
 12. SESSION/ACCESS INVALIDATION (most security-critical):
       - Admin deactivates a user -> that user's existing token -> 400 next request.
       - Demote manager->member -> their next GET /users/ -> 403 (reflects immediately, cache invalidated).
       - Promote member->manager -> next GET /users/ -> 200.
 13. is_superuser back-compat: user created with is_superuser=True has super perm + admin role +
     computed is_superuser True; a plain user has is_superuser False.
 14. Cache unit test: resolve_permissions caches; invalidate_user forces a fresh resolve; TTL default < 300s.

Then: run the new tests to capture the RED checklist and send an interim Report to fsf-main
listing the new tests and pass/fail, confirming the existing 58 tests still pass. Then IMPLEMENT
to green: models, alembic migration (down_revision fe56fa70289e), core/permissions.py cache,
deps.require_permission, route gating, GET /roles/, GET /metrics/ stub, dev-only demo user seed
in initial_data.py (manager@example.com + member@example.com, password changethis, idempotent).

MUST keep the full existing suite green. Update an existing test ONLY if the contract genuinely
changed, and justify it in your report. Before finishing run: ruff, ty/mypy if configured, and
FASTAPI_ENV=development uv run pytest tests/ -q. Re-seed initial data if you wipe the dev DB.

REPORT BACK: files changed, the migration revision id, the final test counts, any contract
deviation, and the exact commands to run the tests. Do NOT git commit unless fsf-main asks.

import uuid

def get_datetime_utc() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(UTC)

    email: EmailStr = Field(unique=True, index=True, max_length=255)
    is_active: bool = True
    is_superuser: bool = False
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


# Properties to receive via API on creation
class UserCreate(UserBase):
    password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)


class UserRegister(SQLModel):
    email: EmailStr = Field(max_length=255)
    password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


# Properties to receive via API on update, all are optional
class UserUpdate(SQLModel):
    email: EmailStr | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    is_active: bool | None = None
    is_superuser: bool | None = None
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    password: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=8, max_length=128)


class UserUpdateMe(SQLModel):
    full_name: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)
    email: EmailStr | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255)


class UpdatePassword(SQLModel):
    current_password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)
    new_password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=128)


# Database model, database table inferred from class name
class User(UserBase, table=True):
    id: uuid.UUID = Field(default_factory=uuid.uuid4, primary_key=True)
    hashed_password: str
    created_at: datetime | None = Field(default_factory=get_datetime_utc)
    items: list[Item] = Relationship(back_populates="owner", cascade_delete=True)


# Properties to return via API, id is always required

class UsersPublic(SQLModel):

    title: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=255)

    title: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=255)

import uuid
from typing import Any

from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app.core.security import get_password_hash, verify_password
from app.models import Item, ItemCreate, User, UserCreate, UserUpdate


def create_user(*, session: Session, user_create: UserCreate) -> User:
    db_obj = User.model_validate(
        user_create, update={"hashed_password": get_password_hash(user_create.password)}
    )
    session.add(db_obj)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_obj)
    return db_obj


def update_user(*, session: Session, db_user: User, user_in: UserUpdate) -> Any:
    user_data = user_in.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    extra_data = {}
    if "password" in user_data:
        password = user_data["password"]
        hashed_password = get_password_hash(password)
        extra_data["hashed_password"] = hashed_password
    db_user.sqlmodel_update(user_data, update=extra_data)
    session.add(db_user)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_user)
    return db_user


def get_user_by_email(*, session: Session, email: str) -> User | None:
    statement = select(User).where(User.email == email)
    session_user = session.exec(statement).first()
    return session_user


# Dummy hash to use for timing attack prevention when user is not found
# This is an Argon2 hash of a random password, used to ensure constant-time comparison
DUMMY_HASH = "$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=4$MjQyZWE1MzBjYjJlZTI0Yw$YTU4NGM5ZTZmYjE2NzZlZjY0ZWY3ZGRkY2U2OWFjNjk"


def authenticate(*, session: Session, email: str, password: str) -> User | None:
    db_user = get_user_by_email(session=session, email=email)
    if not db_user:
        # Prevent timing attacks by running password verification even when user doesn't exist
        # This ensures the response time is similar whether or not the email exists
        verify_password(password, DUMMY_HASH)
        return None
    verified, updated_password_hash = verify_password(password, db_user.hashed_password)
    if not verified:
        return None
    if updated_password_hash:
        db_user.hashed_password = updated_password_hash
        session.add(db_user)
        session.commit()
        session.refresh(db_user)
    return db_user


def create_item(*, session: Session, item_in: ItemCreate, owner_id: uuid.UUID) -> Item:
    db_item = Item.model_validate(item_in, update={"owner_id": owner_id})
    session.add(db_item)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_item)
    return db_item

from collections.abc import Generator
from typing import Annotated

import jwt
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer
from jwt.exceptions import InvalidTokenError
from pydantic import ValidationError
from sqlmodel import Session

from app.core import security
from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.db import engine
from app.models import TokenPayload, User

reusable_oauth2 = OAuth2PasswordBearer(
    tokenUrl=f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/login/access-token"
)


def get_db() -> Generator[Session]:
    with Session(engine) as session:
        yield session


SessionDep = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)]
TokenDep = Annotated[str, Depends(reusable_oauth2)]


def get_current_user(session: SessionDep, token: TokenDep) -> User:
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            token, settings.SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[security.ALGORITHM]
        )
        token_data = TokenPayload(**payload)
    except InvalidTokenError, ValidationError:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="Could not validate credentials",
        )
    user = session.get(User, token_data.sub)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="User not found")
    if not user.is_active:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Inactive user")
    return user


CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)]


def get_current_active_superuser(current_user: CurrentUser) -> User:
    if not current_user.is_superuser:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403, detail="The user doesn't have enough privileges"
        )
    return current_user

import warnings
from typing import Literal, Self

from pydantic import (
    EmailStr,
    HttpUrl,
    PostgresDsn,
    computed_field,
    field_validator,
    model_validator,
)
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        # Use top level .env file (one level above ./backend/)
        env_file="../.env",
        env_ignore_empty=True,
        extra="ignore",
    )
    API_V1_STR: str = "/api/v1"
    SECRET_KEY: str
    # 60 minutes * 24 hours * 8 days = 8 days
    ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES: int = 60 * 24 * 8
    FRONTEND_HOST: str = "http://localhost:5173"
    FASTAPI_ENV: Literal["development"] | None = None

    PROJECT_NAME: str
    SENTRY_DSN: HttpUrl | None = None
    DATABASE_URL: PostgresDsn

    @field_validator("DATABASE_URL", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _use_psycopg_driver(cls, value: str | PostgresDsn) -> str:
        database_url = str(value)
        for scheme in ("postgres://", "postgresql://"):
            if database_url.startswith(scheme):
                return database_url.replace(scheme, "postgresql+psycopg://", 1)
        return database_url

    SMTP_TLS: bool = True
    SMTP_SSL: bool = False
    SMTP_PORT: int = 587
    SMTP_HOST: str | None = None
    SMTP_USER: str | None = None
    SMTP_PASSWORD: str | None = None
    EMAILS_FROM_EMAIL: EmailStr | None = None
    EMAILS_FROM_NAME: str | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _set_default_emails_from(self) -> Self:
        if not self.EMAILS_FROM_NAME:
            self.EMAILS_FROM_NAME = self.PROJECT_NAME
        return self

    EMAIL_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRE_HOURS: int = 48

    @computed_field  # type: ignore[prop-decorator]
    @property
    def emails_enabled(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.SMTP_HOST and self.EMAILS_FROM_EMAIL)

    EMAIL_TEST_USER: EmailStr = "test@example.com"
    FIRST_SUPERUSER: EmailStr
    FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD: str

    def _check_default_secret(self, var_name: str, value: str | None) -> None:
        if value == "changethis":
            message = (
                f'The value of {var_name} is "changethis", '
                "for security, please change it, at least for deployments."
            )
            if self.FASTAPI_ENV == "development":
                warnings.warn(message, stacklevel=1)
            else:
                raise ValueError(message)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _enforce_non_default_secrets(self) -> Self:
        self._check_default_secret("SECRET_KEY", self.SECRET_KEY)
        for host in self.DATABASE_URL.hosts():
            self._check_default_secret("DATABASE_URL password", host["password"])
        self._check_default_secret(
            "FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD", self.FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD
        )

        return self


settings = Settings()  # type: ignore # ty: ignore[unused-ignore-comment]

from app import crud
from app.core.config import settings
from app.models import User, UserCreate

engine = create_engine(str(settings.DATABASE_URL), pool_pre_ping=True)


# make sure all SQLModel models are imported (app.models) before initializing DB
# otherwise, SQLModel might fail to initialize relationships properly
# for more details: https://github.com/fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template/issues/28


def init_db(session: Session) -> None:
    # Tables should be created with Alembic migrations
    # But if you don't want to use migrations, create
    # the tables un-commenting the next lines
    # from sqlmodel import SQLModel

    # This works because the models are already imported and registered from app.models
    # SQLModel.metadata.create_all(engine)

    user = session.exec(
        select(User).where(User.email == settings.FIRST_SUPERUSER)
    ).first()
    if not user:
        user_in = UserCreate(
            email=settings.FIRST_SUPERUSER,
            password=settings.FIRST_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD,
            is_superuser=True,
        )
        user = crud.create_user(session=session, user_create=user_in)

from pydantic import ValidationError

)

def get_current_user(session: SessionDep, token: TokenDep) -> User:
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            token, settings.SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[security.ALGORITHM]
        )
        token_data = TokenPayload(**payload)
    except InvalidTokenError, ValidationError:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="Could not validate credentials",
        )
    user = session.get(User, token_data.sub)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="User not found")
    if not user.is_active:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Inactive user")
    return user

    # Create a bcrypt hash directly (simulating legacy password)

    bcrypt_hash = bcrypt_hasher.hash(password)

    # Create user with bcrypt hash directly in the database
    user = User(email=email, hashed_password=bcrypt_hash)
    db.add(user)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(user)

    # Verify the hash is bcrypt before authentication
    assert user.hashed_password.startswith("$2")

    # Authenticate - this should upgrade the hash to argon2
    authenticated_user = crud.authenticate(session=db, email=email, password=password)
    assert authenticated_user
    assert authenticated_user.email == email

    db.refresh(authenticated_user)

    # Verify the hash was upgraded to argon2
    assert authenticated_user.hashed_password.startswith("$argon2")

    verified, updated_hash = verify_password(
        password, authenticated_user.hashed_password
    )
    assert verified
    # Should not need another update since it's already argon2
    assert updated_hash is None

test_rbac = r'''"""RBAC contract test suite.

This is the strict checklist for the role <-> permission access-control feature
described in the parent task's LOCKED ARCHITECTURE. Each test maps to a numbered
checklist item.

Roles / permission sets under test:
  admin   -> {super, users:read, users:manage, metrics:read}
  manager -> {users:read, metrics:read}
  member  -> {}   (self-service only)
"""

import uuid

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlmodel import Session

from app.core.config import settings
from tests.utils.user import (
    create_user_with_roles,
    get_role_by_name,
    role_headers,
)
from tests.utils.utils import random_email, random_lower_string

API = settings.API_V1_STR

EXPECTED_ROLE_PERMS = {
    "admin": {"super", "users:read", "users:manage", "metrics:read"},
    "manager": {"users:read", "metrics:read"},
    "member": set(),
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Seed integrity
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_seed_roles_and_permissions(db: Session) -> None:
    for role_name, expected in EXPECTED_ROLE_PERMS.items():
        role = get_role_by_name(session=db, name=role_name)
        assert role is not None, f"role {role_name} missing"
        actual = {p.name for p in role.permissions}
        assert actual == expected, f"{role_name}: {actual} != {expected}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. /users/me exposes roles + permissions + computed is_superuser
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_users_me_exposes_roles_permissions(client: TestClient, db: Session) -> None:
    for role_name, expected_perms in EXPECTED_ROLE_PERMS.items():
        _, headers = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=[role_name])
        r = client.get(f"{API}/users/me", headers=headers)
        assert r.status_code == 200
        body = r.json()
        assert body["roles"] == [role_name]
        assert set(body["permissions"]) == expected_perms
        assert body["is_superuser"] is (role_name == "admin")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. GET /users/ : admin 200, manager 200, member 403, anon 401
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_list_users_authorization(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: dict[str, str]
) -> None:
    _, manager = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["manager"])
    _, member = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["member"])

    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/", headers=superuser_token_headers).status_code == 200
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/", headers=manager).status_code == 200
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/", headers=member).status_code == 403
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/").status_code == 401


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. POST /users/ : admin ok, manager 403, member 403
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_create_user_authorization(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: dict[str, str]
) -> None:
    _, manager = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["manager"])
    _, member = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["member"])

    payload = {"email": random_email(), "password": random_lower_string()}
    r = client.post(f"{API}/users/", headers=superuser_token_headers, json=payload)
    assert 200 <= r.status_code < 300

    assert client.post(
        f"{API}/users/", headers=manager,
        json={"email": random_email(), "password": random_lower_string()},
    ).status_code == 403
    assert client.post(
        f"{API}/users/", headers=member,
        json={"email": random_email(), "password": random_lower_string()},
    ).status_code == 403


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. PATCH /users/{id} : admin ok, manager 403, member 403
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_patch_user_authorization(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: dict[str, str]
) -> None:
    target, _ = create_user_with_roles(session=db, role_names=["member"])
    _, manager = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["manager"])
    _, member = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["member"])

    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{target.id}", headers=superuser_token_headers,
        json={"full_name": "Renamed"},
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{target.id}", headers=manager, json={"full_name": "x"}
    ).status_code == 403
    assert client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{target.id}", headers=member, json={"full_name": "x"}
    ).status_code == 403


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. DELETE /users/{id} : admin ok, manager 403, member 403
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_delete_user_authorization(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: dict[str, str]
) -> None:
    _, manager = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["manager"])
    _, member = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["member"])

    victim, _ = create_user_with_roles(session=db, role_names=["member"])
    assert client.delete(
        f"{API}/users/{victim.id}", headers=manager
    ).status_code == 403
    assert client.delete(
        f"{API}/users/{victim.id}", headers=member
    ).status_code == 403

    r = client.delete(f"{API}/users/{victim.id}", headers=superuser_token_headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. GET /users/{id} : self 200 for all; other-user admin/manager 200, member 403
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_get_user_by_id_authorization(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: dict[str, str]
) -> None:
    admin_user = None
    admin_me = client.get(f"{API}/users/me", headers=superuser_token_headers).json()
    admin_id = admin_me["id"]

    manager_user, manager = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["manager"])
    member_user, member = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["member"])
    other, _ = create_user_with_roles(session=db, role_names=["member"])

    # self always OK
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/{admin_id}", headers=superuser_token_headers).status_code == 200
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/{manager_user.id}", headers=manager).status_code == 200
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/{member_user.id}", headers=member).status_code == 200

    # other-user
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/{other.id}", headers=superuser_token_headers).status_code == 200
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/{other.id}", headers=manager).status_code == 200
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/{other.id}", headers=member).status_code == 403


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Role assignment via role_ids (users:manage) + no self-escalation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_admin_assigns_roles_via_role_ids(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: dict[str, str]
) -> None:
    target, _ = create_user_with_roles(session=db, role_names=["member"])
    manager_role = get_role_by_name(session=db, name="manager")
    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{target.id}", headers=superuser_token_headers,
        json={"role_ids": [str(manager_role.id)]},
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json()["roles"] == ["manager"]


def test_manager_cannot_escalate_self_to_admin(
    client: TestClient, db: Session
) -> None:
    manager_user, manager = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["manager"])
    admin_role = get_role_by_name(session=db, name="admin")
    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{manager_user.id}", headers=manager,
        json={"role_ids": [str(admin_role.id)]},
    )
    assert r.status_code == 403
    # still not a superuser
    me = client.get(f"{API}/users/me", headers=manager).json()
    assert me["is_superuser"] is False
    assert "super" not in me["permissions"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. GET /metrics/ : admin 200, manager 200, member 403, anon 401
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_metrics_authorization(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: dict[str, str]
) -> None:
    _, manager = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["manager"])
    _, member = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["member"])

    r = client.get(f"{API}/metrics/", headers=superuser_token_headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert "total_users" in body
    assert "active_users" in body
    assert "users_per_role" in body

    assert client.get(f"{API}/metrics/", headers=manager).status_code == 200
    assert client.get(f"{API}/metrics/", headers=member).status_code == 403
    assert client.get(f"{API}/metrics/").status_code == 401


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  GET /roles/ : users:read (admin + manager); member 403; anon 401
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_roles_endpoint_authorization(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: dict[str, str]
) -> None:
    _, manager = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["manager"])
    _, member = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["member"])

    r = client.get(f"{API}/roles/", headers=superuser_token_headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    names = {row["name"] for row in r.json()["data"]}
    assert {"admin", "manager", "member"} <= names

    assert client.get(f"{API}/roles/", headers=manager).status_code == 200
    assert client.get(f"{API}/roles/", headers=member).status_code == 403
    assert client.get(f"{API}/roles/").status_code == 401


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Member self-service is preserved
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_member_self_service(client: TestClient, db: Session) -> None:
    user, password = create_user_with_roles(session=db, role_names=["member"])
    from tests.utils.user import auth_headers_for_user

    headers = auth_headers_for_user(client=client, email=user.email, password=password)

    # GET /users/me
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/me", headers=headers).status_code == 200

    # PATCH /users/me
    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/me", headers=headers, json={"full_name": "Member Name"}
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json()["full_name"] == "Member Name"

    # change own password
    new_password = random_lower_string()
    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/me/password", headers=headers,
        json={"current_password": password, "new_password": new_password},
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    headers = auth_headers_for_user(
        client=client, email=user.email, password=new_password
    )

    # own items CRUD
    r = client.post(f"{API}/items/", headers=headers, json={"title": "mine"})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    item_id = r.json()["id"]
    assert client.get(f"{API}/items/{item_id}", headers=headers).status_code == 200
    assert client.put(
        f"{API}/items/{item_id}", headers=headers, json={"title": "mine2"}
    ).status_code == 200
    assert client.delete(f"{API}/items/{item_id}", headers=headers).status_code == 200


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. PATCH /users/me cannot change role / permission / is_superuser
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_patch_users_me_cannot_change_privileges(
    client: TestClient, db: Session
) -> None:
    user, headers = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["member"])
    manager_role = get_role_by_name(session=db, name="manager")

    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/me",
        headers=headers,
        json={
            "full_name": "Still Member",
            "is_superuser": True,
            "role_ids": [str(manager_role.id)],
            "permissions": ["super"],
            "roles": ["admin"],
        },
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["full_name"] == "Still Member"
    assert body["is_superuser"] is False
    assert body["roles"] == ["member"]
    assert body["permissions"] == []


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Session / access invalidation (most security-critical)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_deactivation_invalidates_existing_token(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: dict[str, str]
) -> None:
    user, headers = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["member"])
    # token works
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/me", headers=headers).status_code == 200
    # admin deactivates
    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{user.id}", headers=superuser_token_headers,
        json={"is_active": False},
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    # existing token now rejected (inactive user)
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/me", headers=headers).status_code == 400


def test_demote_manager_reflects_immediately(
    client: TestClient, db: Session, superuser_token_headers: dict[str, str]
) -> None:
    user, headers = role_headers(client=client, session=db, role_names=["manager"])
    member_role = get_role_by_name(session=db, name="member")
    # manager can list users -> populates cache
    assert client.get(f"{API}/users/", headers=headers).status_code == 200
    # admin demotes to member
    r = client.patch(
        f"{API}/users/{user.id}", headers=superuser_token_headers,
        json={"role_ids": [str(member_role.id)]},
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200

def test_promote_member_reflects_immediately(

def test_unknown_user_id_type(client: TestClient) -> None:

perm_mod = '''"""Short-lived, in-process permission cache.

Resolves the set of permission names granted to a user (via their roles) and
caches it for a short TTL so that repeated authorization checks within the same
request burst do not re-walk the role/permission relationships every time.

Invalidation is explicit: any change that can affect a user's effective
permissions (role assignment change, deactivation, deletion, update) calls
:func:`invalidate_user`; role->permission changes call :func:`invalidate_all`.

LIMITATION: the cache is per-process. Under a multi-worker / multi-process
deployment each worker keeps its own copy, so an invalidation in one worker is
not seen by the others; stale entries would still expire within the TTL. A
cross-process deployment would need a shared store (e.g. Redis) and a pub/sub
invalidation channel. That is intentionally out of scope here.
"""

import threading
import time
import uuid

from sqlmodel import Session

from app.core.config import settings
from app.models import User

# user_id -> (frozenset of permission names, monotonic expiry timestamp)
_cache: dict[uuid.UUID, tuple[frozenset[str], float]] = {}
_lock = threading.Lock()


def _resolve_from_db(user: User) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Walk the user's roles/permissions relationships to the permission names."""
    return frozenset(user.permission_names)


def resolve_permissions(session: Session, user: User) -> set[str]:
    """Return the user's effective permission names, served through the cache.

    ``session`` is accepted for a uniform signature and to keep the user's
    relationships loadable; resolution reads the ORM relationships directly.
    """
    now = time.monotonic()
    user_id = user.id
    with _lock:
        entry = _cache.get(user_id)
        if entry is not None and entry[1] > now:
            return set(entry[0])

    perms = _resolve_from_db(user)
    expires_at = time.monotonic() + settings.PERMISSIONS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS
    with _lock:
        _cache[user_id] = (perms, expires_at)
    return set(perms)


def invalidate_user(user_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
    """Drop one user's cached permission set (role change, deactivation, ...)."""
    with _lock:
        _cache.pop(user_id, None)


def invalidate_all() -> None:
    """Drop every cached entry (role->permission mapping changed)."""
    with _lock:
        _cache.clear()
'''

## Summary

Built the backend RBAC feature test-first, to the parent's locked architecture.

**Test counts**
- Baseline (pristine tree): **58 passed**
- New tests authored: **21** (RED at checkpoint — `ImportError: cannot import name 'Role'`, 0 passing, the intended test-first red)
- Final: **79 passed** (58 existing + 21 new), `scripts/lint.sh` exit 0 (mypy strict, ty, ruff check, ruff format)

**Exact commands** (from `backend/`)
- `FASTAPI_ENV=development uv run pytest tests/ -q`
- `FASTAPI_ENV=development uv run pytest tests/api/routes/test_rbac.py tests/core/test_permissions_cache.py -q`
- `uv run bash scripts/lint.sh`

**Migration:** `3c2a211a9237` (down_revision `fe56fa70289e`) — creates permission/role/rolepermission/userrole (FKs `ON DELETE CASCADE`), seeds 4 permissions + 3 roles + links, backfills `userrole` from `user.is_superuser`, then drops the column. Round-trip (upgrade→downgrade→upgrade on a populated DB) verified to preserve the super↔admin mapping.

**Files changed**
- Modified: `app/models.py`, `app/crud.py`, `app/api/deps.py`, `app/api/routes/users.py`, `app/api/main.py`, `app/core/config.py`, `app/core/db.py`, `tests/utils/user.py` (helpers *added*, no existing helper changed)
- New: `app/core/permissions.py`, `app/api/routes/roles.py`, `app/api/routes/metrics.py`, `app/alembic/versions/3c2a211a9237_rbac_roles_permissions.py`, `tests/api/routes/test_rbac.py`, `tests/core/__init__.py`, `tests/core/test_permissions_cache.py`
- Not mine: `../.env` (pre-existing), `backend/server.log` (hive app's own startup log, written when I restarted it)

**Contract deviations:** none. No existing test modified; `is_superuser` back-compat kept via a computed property.

**Live:** migration applied to the dev DB (:8071), initial data re-seeded (the pytest teardown wipes users), and the hive `app` restarted (it 500'd on old code against the new schema until restart). Verified on http://full-stack-fastapi.adi — admin/manager/member logins, `/users/me`, `/metrics/`, `/roles/`, and 403/401 enforcement all correct. Three demo logins: `admin@`/`manager@`/`member@example.com`, password `changethis`.

**Handoff to fsf-frontend:** the OpenAPI surface changed (new `GET /roles/`, `GET /metrics/`; `UserPublic` now returns `roles[]`, `permissions[]`, computed `is_superuser`; `UserCreate`/`UserUpdate` accept `role_ids`) — regenerate the client with `bash scripts/generate-client.sh` from the repo root.
